Challenge 1: The Hadwiger Conjecture

Definition 1 (Hadwiger Number).

Given a graph G, the Hadwiger number of G is the largest integer t such that the complete graph Kt on t vertices is a minor of G. We denote the Hadwiger number by h⁢(G).

Conjecture 1.1 (Hadwiger’s Conjecture [2, Conjecture 1]).

Let r∈ℕ. For every finite simple graph G, we have:

h⁢(G)≤r⟹χ⁢(G)≤r

where χ⁢(G) denotes the chromatic number of G.

While Conjecture 1.1 is not too difficult for values of r≤3, already for r=4 it is equivalent to the 4-colour theorem. Robertson, Seymour and Thomas proved the above for r=5 [1].

References

  • [1] N. Robertson, P. Seymour, and R. Thomas (1993) Hadwiger’s conjecture for K6-free graphs. Combinatorica 13, pp. 279–361. doi: 10.1007/BF01202354.
  • [2] R. Steiner (2024) Hadwiger’s conjecture and topological bounds. European Journal of Combinatorics 122, pp. 104033. doi: 10.1016/j.ejc.2024.104033.
